subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native no-third-party browser-held E2EE chat in core, or first define Gateway/plugin seams for an external encrypted browser transport?
rationale: The request changes encryption, browser/device trust, transcript visibility, key lifecycle, routing isolation, and relay fallback boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve design-first core capability
options.body: Define the threat model, encrypted envelope protocol, key lifecycle, transcript semantics, and Gateway/Control UI contracts before any implementation branch.

options.title: Make it plugin-first
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only the missing Gateway/plugin SDK seams needed for an external encrypted browser transport to integrate safely.

options.title: Defer native transport
options.body: Keep WebChat, Tailscale, third-party channels, and dmScope isolation as the supported paths until maintainers explicitly accept this direction.

recommendation.title: Approve design-first core capability
recommendation.body: Define the threat model, encrypted envelope protocol, key lifecycle, transcript semantics, and Gateway/Control UI contracts before any implementation branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is primarily an encryption/key ownership and transcript visibility boundary, with WebChat product ownership following after the security model is accepted.
